what: Curated carve plan for Spengel, Rhetores Graeci vol. III, served whole under one treatise's urn (issue #22); consumed by scripts/carve_edition_volume.py
boundary_form: Same as the Walz plan: a work carries a START locus and no end, so the partition is exact by construction.

volumes.edition_title: Rhetores Graeci, vol. III, ed. L. Spengel (Leipzig, Teubner, 1856)
volumes.offset_note: printed = scan - 46 at the start of the body, and the zones step the offset up by exactly the number of leaves dropped before them: 10 at the Demetrius repeat, 12 more at the Menander repeat, 7 and 8 in Nicolaus and the index. So there is really one offset and four repeated signatures, not five offsets. Dropping a scan removes it from the output but does not renumber the pages after it, which is why the drop has to be paid for in the zones as well. All nineteen ARGUMENTUM page numbers then land exactly on their display title, which is nineteen independent checks on the model.
volumes.drop_scans_note: Second copies of repeated signatures, confirmed by vocabulary overlap against the first copy (jaccard 0.65-0.89) and by the second copy being the worse OCR: scan 528 has lost every accent its twin at 520 still carries. Archived verbatim in the audit.
volumes.basis: The ARGUMENTUM at scan 46 lists all nineteen items, numbered XVIII-XXXVI, each with its printed page range. That is the boundary source; every start was then verified at the row against the display title.
volumes.front_matter_note: scans 7-46, printed by roman numeral: Spengel's Latin praefatio and adnotationes, and the ARGUMENTUM itself. 4,060 tokens. Left in the volume file, like the Walz roman-numbered front matter, because the printed-page locus scheme has no way to express a roman folio.
volumes.trailing_residual_note: printed 499 onward is the index of terms over the whole Rhetores Graeci ('ἀντικατάστασις I, 366, 26; II, 146, 14'), 2,064 tokens. It indexes every volume, not this one, so it belongs to no work here.
volumes.disposition_note: Eighteen of the nineteen are already served, five from First1KGreek and thirteen from our own OCR of Walz VIII, Roberts or Felten, so under the decision in issue #14 they are filed as secondary witnesses. That is the finding rather than a compromise: Spengel III and Walz VIII print substantially the same corpus of figure and trope treatises, which the 4-gram overlap confirms at 46-55% per work. Only item XVIII is served as primary, because nothing in the corpus matches it.

works.title: Ek ton Alexandrou (excerpts on thesis and hypothesis)
works.evidence: ARGUMENTUM entry XVIII, printed 1-6. No display title: the volume opens straight into the text at printed 1, and the ARGUMENTUM is the boundary source. Its 4-grams match nothing else in the corpus, which is why it is the one item here served as primary.
works.author_note: Spengel prints it as excerpts 'from the works of Alexander' rather than as a work of his, so the slug records the excerpt, not an attribution.
works.incipit_note: Anchored below the initial capital on purpose: the OCR reads the alpha of Ἀλέξανδρος as a Latin A, so an anchor that included it would fail on a homoglyph rather than on a boundary.
